This repo is a Flask-like package named `tessel`. All the relevant code is in `src/tessel/views.py`.

**Class → view function**
- `View.to_view_func(name, *class_args, **class_kwargs)` (line 86) is a classmethod that builds a closure `view(**kwargs)`.
- With `init_every_request = True` (the default), `view` instantiates `view.view_class(...)` on each request and calls `self.run_view(**kwargs)`. When it is `False`, one shared instance is reused.
- Calls go through `active_app.ensure_sync(...)`.
- The function gets `view_class`, `__name__`, `__doc__`, `methods` and `provide_automatic_options` attached (lines 129–134). It is also wrapped by any `cls.decorators`.
- You register it with `app.attach_route_rule(path, view_func=Cls.to_view_func("name"))`.

**Per-method routing: `VerbView`** (line 138, subclasses `View`)
- `VerbView.__init_subclass__` (line 165) builds `cls.methods`. It starts from the base classes' `methods`, then adds the uppercase name of every entry in `http_method_funcs` (line 11) that the class defines, such as `get` and `post`. This is what the route registers as its allowed methods.
- `VerbView.run_view` (line 182) does the dispatch. It looks up `getattr(self, request.method.lower())` and calls it with the URL kwargs. `HEAD` falls back to `get` when there is no `head` handler.
